additionalQuestions.disqualifyMessage: Florida home studies are only available to Florida residents. If you live in another state, please contact a licensed adoption agency in your state of residence.

additionalQuestions.disqualifyMessage: Florida requires FDLE and FBI fingerprint background checks for all household members age 12 and older, plus a DCF central abuse registry review. Visit our preparation resources to learn how to get started.

additionalQuestions.disqualifyMessage: Florida home studies require current pet vaccination records. Please get your pets vaccinated and obtain documentation before applying.

additionalQuestions.question: Are you at least 10 years older than the child you are hoping to adopt?
additionalQuestions.why: California law (Fam. Code § 8601) requires adoptive parents to be at least 10 years older than the child, with limited exceptions for stepparents and close relatives.
additionalQuestions.disqualifyMessage: California law generally requires adoptive parents to be at least 10 years older than the child. Exceptions exist for stepparents, siblings, aunts, uncles, and first cousins. If you believe an exception applies to your situation, speak with a licensed California adoption attorney.
nextSteps: Consider whether a stepparent or close-relative exception applies to you
Speak with a licensed California adoption attorney about your options

additionalQuestions.question: Are all adults in your household prepared to submit fingerprints for a California DOJ and FBI background check?
additionalQuestions.why: California requires fingerprint-based background checks from the CA Department of Justice and the FBI for all adults in the household.
additionalQuestions.disqualifyMessage: California requires fingerprint-based background checks from the CA Department of Justice and the FBI for all adults in the home. Visit our preparation resources to learn how to complete this step.
nextSteps: Talk with the adults in your household about the fingerprinting requirement
Review the Documentation Checklist below for what the background check involves

additionalQuestions.question: If your home has a swimming pool or spa, does it have at least one approved safety barrier (e.g., an isolation fence, alarmed door/window, or pool alarm)?
additionalQuestions.why: California's Swimming Pool Safety Act imposes stricter pool safety requirements than most other states.
additionalQuestions.naLabel: My home does not have a pool or spa
additionalQuestions.disqualifyMessage: California law requires pools and spas to have at least one approved safety barrier. Common solutions include an isolation fence or alarmed doors and windows that access the pool. Review our home preparation guide for details.
nextSteps: Get a quote for an isolation fence or approved pool alarm
Work through the Prepare Your Home checklist below before your home visit
